title: N.K.V. Bros. (P) Ltd. v. M. Karumai Ammal
holding: Motor accident compensation proceedings should adopt a practical approach and not defeat genuine claims through technicalities where negligence and loss are reasonably established.

title: Sarla Verma v. Delhi Transport Corporation
holding: The Court standardized the multiplier approach and key compensation principles for fatal and injury motor accident claims.

title: Arnesh Kumar v. State of Bihar
holding: Arrest is not automatic for offences punishable up to seven years; police must justify necessity and comply with statutory safeguards.

title: Satender Kumar Antil v. CBI
holding: Bail jurisprudence must protect personal liberty and reduce unnecessary incarceration, especially where arrest was not required during investigation.

title: Lucknow Development Authority v. M.K. Gupta
holding: Public authorities and service providers can be liable for deficiency in service under consumer law where consumers suffer loss or harassment.

title: Indian Medical Association v. V.P. Shantha
holding: Medical services fall within consumer protection law in many situations, allowing patients to seek redress for deficient service.

title: Kailash Nath Associates v. Delhi Development Authority
holding: Compensation clauses are subject to reasonableness and actual legal injury; statutory damages principles cannot be applied mechanically.

title: K.S. Vidyanadam v. Vairavan
holding: Specific performance is discretionary and delay or inequitable conduct can affect relief even where a contract exists.

title: Suraj Lamp & Industries Pvt. Ltd. v. State of Haryana
holding: GPA sales and similar informal arrangements do not by themselves convey legal title to immovable property.

title: K.S. Puttaswamy v. Union of India
holding: Privacy is a fundamental right and state or institutional action affecting privacy must satisfy constitutional standards.
